usual_baseline: CT KUB within target is usually good, 93–100% [2359][2440][2471][2667], but not everywhere (335 of 705 within 14 hours [2249]). Serum calcium 21–51% [2667][2440][2600], urate 2.6–4%, NSAIDs 52–55% [2440][2471], dietary advice 8.7–17% [2471][2600].
fix_that_works: Renal order-set and stone diet leaflet: calcium 77.9% to 94.7%, NSAIDs 54.5% to 71.9%, dietary advice 8.7% to 39.4% [2471]. Email reminders and a handover-sheet note: calcium 21% to 72% [2667]. Hot URS theatre: treatment within 48 hours 35% to 53%, dietary advice 17% to 72% [2600].
fix_that_fails: Updated NSAID dosing and pathway: NSAIDs fell 87% to 50% on six patients [2359]. After teaching, only 26.4% were seen in clinic within 4 weeks [2026]. Dietary advice stayed low at 39.4% [2471].
consultant_advice: CT timing is done and usually met; don't audit it again. Audit what happens after the ED: time to definitive treatment, stent use without indication, and follow-up clinic waits. Use an order-set for calcium.
